transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2026-08-25
- Start: 09:30 PDT
- Duration: 1h15m (approx)
- Attendees: Aisha (PM), Jonah (Eng Lead), Priya (SRE), Marco (Product Ops), Samir (QA), Eileen (VP Product), Diego (Head of Deployments), Nora (Compliance)
- Recording: fireflies.ai link omitted

Summary: quick handoff of the launch contract and incident/playbook ownership for the upcoming dedicated-region rollout; primary focus on who owns fallback behaviors and the runbooks for KV/cache eviction, model routing fallbacks, and private deployment SSO gating.

Topics: rollout timeline, SLOs for canary, staged fallback triggers, audit log requirements, oncall rotation for first 72 hours, where to store final artifact (Confluence vs. shared drive), and brief incident postmortem expectations.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Aisha): ok everyone thanks for joining, i'll keep this tight we have 75 minutes but mostly this is handoff so uh if we can get owners assigned that's the goal
00:18 Jonah (Eng Lead): yeah i'll start with the engineering view, so the canary plan we discussed last week - two control planes: staging and pre-prod, traffic split 5/95, will be running the rex-quantized variant for first 24 hours to save cost, um small caveat i want to call out that the kernel fallback path for long sequences still hasn't hit perf parity so latency may spike under 2% of requests
00:42 Priya (SRE): spike under two percent, okay captured; we need clear SLO burn thresholds for automatic rollback, not just alerts. proposing a 99.5 p50 p95 p99 SLO set?
00:58 Eileen (VP Product): sorry quick interrupt, can you re-state that as a single trigger? like "if p95 latency exceeds 300ms for 10 minutes"?
01:12 Jonah: yeah, that's fair. so proposal: p95 > 300ms sustained for 10 minutes OR error rate > 0.5% sustained 5 minutes triggers immediate rollback and page to infra. i put that in the doc but it's rough.
01:29 Marco (Product Ops): link to the draft playbook is in the meeting notes, filename: rollout_playbook_draft_v3.pdf (shared drive)
01:40 Nora (Compliance): a note on audit logs — we need per-request redaction policy spelled out; KMS envelope wrapping for both hosted and dedicated must be explicit. also SSO assertion retention window, we can't keep raw tokens more than 90 days per policy.
02:05 Aisha: good. so owner for the rollback condition?
02:09 Jonah: engineering owns the automated rollback hook, SRE owns the alerting/monitoring config and oncall paging. i can own the hook but Priya will own runbook steps.
02:22 Priya: confirm. i'll add the runbook steps for manual rollback, emergency fallback to compatible-model routing, and KV eviction checklist. note: "KV eviction" in the doc sometimes shows as kv-cache evict, sometimes kv-cash, so be careful with nomenclature - folks will read it wrong.
02:46 Samir (QA): there's also a regression test we need: end-to-end latency under synthetic LL workload with 1024 tokens for the quant variant. i can run nightly for the canary window.
03:03 Diego (Head of Deployments): on the dedicated side, we need to cap batch sizes to prevent OOMs on rtx-small nodes; has anyone run the batch-stress profile on that exact instance?
03:20 Jonah: partial run. we ran 3/4 of the matrix; the missing piece was the 4096 sequence long tail on multi-turn. that caused a kernel fallback path which spiky latency and once triggered it cascaded to the next worker pool.
03:37 Priya: ok that's a concern. mitigation options: pre-warm a separate long-seq pool or enable soft-eviction policy for KV entries older than 5 minutes for canary traffic; both have tradeoffs for cost and quality.
03:55 Eileen: what about fallback policies — do we prefer model downgrade (smaller model) vs. batching trading latency for throughput? what's the customer-visible impact?
04:10 Jonah: model downgrade is less visible but can change generation characteristics; batching reduces p50 but may increase tail. for product-facing customers we should prefer model downgrade as first fallback for sustained overload, and batching for transient bursts. we should document the degrade ladder.
04:30 Aisha: let's make that explicit in the playbook: ladder step 1: prefix cache hit; step 2: fallback to next-compatible model variant; step 3: staged batching; step 4: full rollback.
04:47 Nora: also flag data residency implications of model downgrade — some customers have region-locked model weights for privacy; we can't route them to a variant outside their region. add that as a gating condition.
05:05 Marco: ops note: we need emergency contact details for our cloud partners; i have AWS and Hyperscale contacts but not the new vendor Nimbus Endpoints. Samir can you follow up?
05:20 Samir: yep i'll reach out and add to the runbook.
05:24 Jonah: quick technical deep-dive — the KV prefix caching logic currently allows up to 10k entries per worker before eviction, threshold tuned for normal traffic. for canary i suggest decreasing to 4k to avoid full memory pressure. downside: more cache misses may increase token costs.
05:46 Priya: that's fine for canary. make sure metrics expose eviction rate, miss rate, and memory headroom. those three are critical for the SRE dashboard.
06:00 Aisha: who will make the dashboard slice?
06:03 Priya: i'll do the SRE slice, Jonah will add labels to the emitted metrics so they can be filtered by deployment tag.
06:13 Diego: on the private deployment customers we have to validate their SAML assertions and also the KMS key policies; Nora, can you confirm the required artifacts for them to sign off?
06:25 Nora: yes: KMS policy template, list of encryption scopes, SOC2 annex A, and network topology diagram. i'll send the template.
06:35 Aisha: include a checklist in the playbook where legal signs off and the customer confirms retention windows. that's non-negotiable.
06:44 Marco: timeline check — the go/no-go gate is 2026-09-02 EOD for canary start on 2026-09-03. we need all runbooks and test matrices done by 2026-08-28 to allow dry-run.
06:58 Jonah: that's tight but doable. we'll prioritize bucket of tests: batch-stress, long-seq tail, quant-fidelity regressions, and SLO burn tests. Samir will coordinate test harness.
07:12 Samir: i'll schedule nightly runs starting 8/26 and share results sheet. note: the harness sometimes reports token alignment errors that look like model hallucinations but are actually seed differences; i'll mark those as noise.
07:30 Eileen: on postmortem expectations — if something goes wrong in the 72 hour window we want a blameless timeline, a preliminary incident timeline within 2 hours, and a full RCA within 5 business days. can we commit?
07:46 Priya: yes SRE will produce the preliminary timeline and severity estimate within 2 hours for any sev2/3 and 30 minutes for sev1; final RCA in 5 business days.
07:58 Nora: compliance wants the incident artifact stored with immutable logs, and we need to keep change history for playbook edits. make sure confluence page has edit locks and versioning.
08:13 Aisha: action owner recap — i'll read them out. Jonah will deliver the degraded-capacity runbook section and the automated rollback hook by 2026-08-26. Priya will create the SLO dashboard slice and oncall pager mappings by 2026-08-27. Marco will gather vendor contacts and finalize the emergency contact table by 2026-08-27. Samir will run nightly test harness and share the sheet by 2026-08-26. Nora will share KMS and SOC2 templates by 2026-08-26.
08:45 Diego: two quick clarifications — where do we store the final signed rollout contract? I prefer internal legal drive not confluence.
08:54 Marco: store the signed pdf in legal-drive/redwood-rollouts and link from confluence; confluence will be the living runbook.
09:05 Aisha: perfect. last thing: communications plan — Marketing and Sales need a de-scoped blurb for the beta customers. Marco can you coordinate with Growth?
09:16 Marco: yes i'll draft and share by 8/26.
09:22 Eileen: ok i want to reiterate priority: stability over feature parity for first week. if we have to sacrifice some generation richness pick stability.
09:33 Jonah: agreed.
09:35 Aisha: cool. any final questions?
09:37 (pause)
09:45 Nora: just to note, compliance will need the signed playbook appended to the contract; make sure it's in the template.
09:52 Aisha: noted. thanks everyone. we'll reconvene after the dry-run results next Friday.
09:58 Meeting end.
